records.title: Tamil Nadu: competition, closure and programme-level limits
records.summary: The same award notice records Yokogawa’s evaluated INR 1,139,999,888 and Canarys/Orange INR 1,285,652,986.57 against the winning INR 763,891,408. Programme completion rates outcome Satisfactory but procurement and financial management Moderately Satisfactory; red flags and an unresolved January 2023 incident compensation proceeding are not assigned to this contract.
records.dateBasis: Event/commencement date is distinct from publication, retrieval and later outcome dates; see period.
records.response: No contract-specific adverse judicial finding or respondent denial was verified. Programme-level judicial compensation status is historical; later outcome remains unknown. No outreach occurred.
alternativeExplanations: Lower evaluated price offers an ordinary procurement explanation; bid evaluation is not proof of performance.
Programme red flags cannot identify this recipient as responsible.
records.falsifier: Signed contract, payment certificates, bank statements, specific review findings and later court order would change these conclusions.

records.title: IBRD → India → Tamil Nadu → a flood-monitoring award
records.summary: Loan 8488-IN committed US$400 m to India with an explicit Union→Tamil Nadu→TNUDF route and separate TNUIFSL implementation. A 2022 WRD invitation links loan 84880-IN to flood-monitoring procurement; the 13 March 2023 notification jointly names Azista and SSTECH for one INR 763,891,408 contract. The programme closed 31 March 2023 with US$352,729,993 actually disbursed by IBRD; contractor cash remains unverified.
records.status: loan and award documented; programme closed; company receipts not verified
records.dateBasis: Event/commencement date is distinct from publication, retrieval and later outcome dates; see period.
records.period: Loan 3 June 2015; amendment 30 June 2020; invitation 18 July 2022; award notification 13 March 2023; programme closed 31 March 2023; ICR 22 September 2023
records.response: Response retains comparator bids and mixed programme findings. The state/fund/company/purchaser roles are distinct; full programme disbursement is not attributed to the selected contract.
alternativeExplanations: Co-awarded companies may divide work, but no split is disclosed.
The 2020 removal of credit enhancement and later programme savings can lawfully explain differences between commitment and disbursement.
records.falsifier: Reconcile signed award, amendments, invoices, payment certificates and treasury/bank credits; obtain any contract-specific review before alleging misallocation.

records.title: IDA → India’s budget: actual disbursement with no contractor trace
records.summary: P174027’s SDR 77 m concessional credit 68130 and US$291.4 m non-concessional credit 68120 were approved 15 December 2020. The 2024 ICR reports US$402,601,860 actual disbursement equivalent and closure 31 December 2022. Proceeds enter the Union’s RBI account and Consolidated Fund; the programme document explicitly excludes tracing them to specifically agreed activities.
records.status: closed; disbursement verified at programme level; no specific corporate pass-through
records.dateBasis: Event/commencement date is distinct from publication, retrieval and later outcome dates; see period.
records.response: ICR footnote 1 expressly attributes actual disbursement differing from approval to SDR/USD exchange-rate fluctuation, using WFACS data of 8 April 2024. ICR rates the two-operation series Highly Satisfactory; these are programme assessments, not contractor-payment proof. The legacy raw finance fleet supplied discovery; original PD/ICR were newly retrieved and checked.
alternativeExplanations: The USD 402.60 m actual versus USD 400 m approval reflects mixed currency reporting; the values cannot by themselves establish an overrun.
records.falsifier: Reconcile credit-level withdrawals and FX translation to Treasury receipts; require separate appropriation/payment evidence for any corporate beneficiary claim.

records.title: India and IMF: no outstanding programme credit at 30 September 2026
records.summary: The IMF’s original financial-position table says Outstanding Purchases and Loans: None. It separately records SDR 13,114.40 m quota, SDR 3,532.21 m reserve-tranche position, SDR 16,547.82 m cumulative allocation and SDR 13,720.50 m holdings. Official transaction records contain no 2011–2026 purchase/loan rows; the 2025 Article IV annex corroborates an earlier no-credit snapshot.
records.dateBasis: Event/commencement date is distinct from publication, retrieval and later outcome dates; see period.
records.response: This corrects the retained corpus’s earlier official-source access gap. IMF surveillance and policy advice do not by themselves create a lending instrument. Projected SDR-related charges remain visible and no all-obligations-zero claim is made.
alternativeExplanations: A country can hold SDRs, pay associated charges and undergo Article IV surveillance while having no outstanding programme purchases/loans.
records.falsifier: A later official financial-position table or signed arrangement recording new credit would supersede this dated snapshot.
